Fresh / Heritage

Tomato-Onion Sesame Salad

The simplest bowl on the fresh list: ripe tomato and sweet onion in a soy-sesame dressing, the garden's summer answer to the pickle plate.

Korean · Easy · Serves 4 as banchan

Jump to recipe ↓
Chapter 04 / 10 fresh recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: heritage — the summer garden bowl. The simplest bowl on the fresh list: ripe tomato and sweet onion in a soy-sesame dressing, the garden's summer answer to the pickle plate. It is the tomato plant's one traditional seat at the Korean table — arriving with summer and the garden, staying the season — and the bowl that best accompanies the unmarinated grill records (#M06, #M10), where a clean, juicy, savory-sweet salad is exactly the meat's equal.

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • The onion's cold soak is the whole prep. Ten minutes in ice water takes the raw burn and leaves the sweet — an un-soaked onion runs this bowl; a soaked one supports it. Drain and pat dry.
  • Cut the tomato wedges thick and from a firm-ripe fruit — a soft tomato collapses into the dressing before the table sits.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    The dressing whisked — soy, honey, vinegar, sesame oil — and tasted: it should run lighter than the cabbage family's dressings (#F05), soy present but polite. Checkpoint — the spoon test: bright, mild-savory, the sesame forward. The tomato brings its own acid and sugar; the dressing frames it.
  2. 02
    Wedges and onion folded in with spoons — one gentle turn, the tomatoes bruise at the second — pepper, sesame, scallion over. Checkpoint — the eating test: the wedge's cold burst, the onion's sweet crunch, the dressing's savory line through it. Beside jumulleok (#M06) — plain seared beef — this bowl is the plate's entire garnish department, and it is enough. Chef’s Note — the soy-on-tomato combination is the bowl's small surprise to tables raised on olive oil and balsamic: the soy's umami deepens a ripe tomato the way it deepens everything else, and the sesame oil's nuttiness stands where the West's herbs would. It is not fusion — the summer garden tomato found this treatment in Korean home kitchens decades ago — but it is the bowl on this list most likely to start a conversation at a mixed table.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Bowl flooded pinkSoft tomato or over-tossedFirm-ripe; one turn only
Onion burned hotNo soakThe full 10-minute ice water
Dressing salty against the fruitFull-strength soyA teaspoon of water; a drop more honey
Watery after an hourIt kept — it shouldn'tServe within 2 hours

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Eats within 2 hours; the dressed tomato keeps nothing. Dressing keeps a week.
  • Variations: cucumber wedges alongside the tomato; a few drops of yuja (#F05's jar) for the citrus fork; the same dressing over cold blanched green beans carries the method into autumn.
